text: Anyone who has succeeded in stilling the disturbances of the mind, even the subtle hankerings have been removed, and all the work that person does is for others and not for oneself. If there is such a person, if a person can work towards that, then that person has already climbed ten steps towards the Science of Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: The essence of spiritual practice is that you understand and face that you yourself can use your mind to degrade your mind or raise it up. So, what is the greatest raising up of the mind? When, at least theoretically, you understand that you are not different from the Supreme Brahman, a spark of that reality is in us.
author: Sri M

text: The whole of life is this movement to filling our emptiness, isn’t it?
author: Sri M

text: Most of our life is dependent on public opinion. Is it possible to say that, no matter what anybody says, good or bad, I am actually an essence of the Supreme being which is poorna or full by itself?
author: Sri M

text: Every soul is potentially divine. To make it manifest is the Science of Yoga
author: Sri M

text: If you have a healthy body, you have a healthy mind. If you have a healthy mind then you understand the inner realities. So, therefore, you start with Yogasanas, which gives you a healthy body.
author: Sri M

text: Then you go on to a healthy mind which means what? A mind which is not torn by conflict, a mind which is not disturbed by any distractions whatsoever, which does not overindulge, nor is it steeped in lethargy, a mind which is active but calm, mind that is quiet but sensitive, a mind that is like the ocean, the waves come but they don’t affect you.
author: Sri M

text: . Because what we call mind is our own creation, of images, of experiences, of the past…the projected future. When all this disappears, what remains is not the mind. It’s That. The pure consciousness disassociated with any activity whatsoever. And it’s also the storehouse of all energy.
author: Sri M

text: The whole of our life moves because we seek fullness and happiness, which, unfortunately, we don’t come across so easily.
author: Sri M

text: Disconnected is what we imagine. Not being disconnected is what is the Reality. When you find that which you seek in the outside world, when you find it inside then you realize that there has been no disconnect. That disconnect was also part of your thinking.
author: Sri M

text: The mind is always seeking fulfillment and it has not learned that the fulfillment is inside. So, while it’s still there, keep trying until you can taste a little bit. Once the taste gets into you, then you’ll start seeing that the gap almost disappears little by little.
author: Sri M

text: There are different ways of getting the ‘taste’. One way is to associate with one who is drunk with ‘That’. You associate for some time and you see that ‘hey!, there is something in this guy which I enjoy when I talk with him, I sit with him. Not me, somebody, imaginary. What is it? And then you begin to suspect maybe I can find it in me.
author: Sri M

text: Sometimes it happens spontaneously. You discover, ‘what have I been doing all these years?’ Sometimes it happens because of kindness and compassion. Sometimes it happens because you see somebody's heart is so large. You are giving nothing but the person keeps on giving you something. Then you say, my whole idea of life is all wrong. I need to expand.
author: Sri M

text: You know how limited we make ourselves, thinking that we are limited? Why don’t we for once, at least in the mind, let go of this limitedness and say ‘It can’t be!’. There is the wide world, after all I am just like a speck of sand in this world. Am I so important, or is the world important?
author: Sri M

text: Tantra is defined as Yoga through ‘bhoga’, yoga through enjoyment. That doesn’t mean that Tantra is orgies in the cremation grounds. It means understanding the fact that very few people can get rid of their desires which are an obstacle to the path.
author: Sri M

text: Tantra says that you can get rid of the desire by enjoying it because most people cannot totally get rid of it by abandoning it or avoiding it.
author: Sri M

text: Actually, nobody is so seriously interested in spiritual progress. I have seen hundreds of people; they are ok with spiritual progress as long as it doesn’t interfere with their daily life. If that’s the case, then you need to find a balance between the two. And, the balance depends on different people and different situations.
author: Sri M

text: Moving towards the spiritual journey does not mean that you stop all work. Stopping all work is utter laziness, it has nothing to do with spirituality.
author: Sri M

text: It’s not that work churns you up and meditation makes you inert. It’s not true. Meditation also churns you up, but in a better way, in a different way. And, worldly life churns you up in a different way. So, there are two ways; you need to find out how to link them together.
author: Sri M

text: If you think you will give up work and come to an ashram and live in tranquility and peace, you are completely mistaken. There is no ashram that is tranquil. There is always someone whispering. In fact, when you are in an ashram, it’s a smaller setup so it exaggerates. When there are fewer people, then the politics and differences, everything comes to the forefront, which is good training for spiritual practice.
author: Sri M

text: One should utilize one’s limited intelligence to try and figure out which teacher is suitable for one. Then, take it up, practice sincerely what is being said. Live with the person and find out what’s happening. If you find that it is not taking you on the right path, don’t hesitate to find somebody else. But, this finding somebody else shouldn’t go on forever, because by that time we are dead.
author: Sri M

text: Nobody is perfect. As long as you have a human body some imperfections will be there.
author: Sri M

text: If you have already spiritually advanced during many births and have come to a stage where you need just a little bit of a turn, then, the Guru will choose you. Until then, don’t put your brain into the freezer and say ‘the Guru is going to choose me I’ll do nothing’. Nobody will come.
author: Sri M

text: The fact is that we are separated, and we are looking for it. The puny brain can never find the ‘why’ until it reaches the goal. When it does reach the goal and finds the ‘why’, it cannot explain to someone who is still seeking. But, the fact remains that we are craving. That we cannot deny.
author: Sri M

text: Sadness comes to every human being at some point. We don’t know when it comes or how. It could be that we are deprived of something. It could be because we don’t know where to go. It could be because we are troubled by so many things. All these contribute.
author: Sri M

text: What we usually do when we are sad is to bring on some entertainment so that we are free of it. But that is like sweeping the sadness under the rug. Well, it might be required sometimes, like when you have a headache you take medicine. But that’s temporary and the headache will come back unless you find the root source of the headache.
author: Sri M

text: The root of sadness is that we are not complete, that we are missing something. We feel empty, we feel rejected, therefore we feel dejected. We feel loss of trust all around. We thought ‘this is life’ and we find that it is not. We think that if we do this, this and this I’ll be happy; I did it, but I’m not happy. There are multiple reasons why we feel sad, but the feeling of sadness is common to all human beings.
author: Sri M

text: If you don’t like to enjoy sadness, sometimes you need to survive. So it’s good to sweep it under the rug for some time. But always pick up the rug and see where it is so that you can deal with it on a permanent basis.
author: Sri M

text: The only way to deal with it on a permanent basis is to come face to face with sadness. When you come face to face with it, you will see that it has lost its sting. Then, sadness becomes your friend and it can no longer threaten you. You are always happy.
author: Sri M

text: Sometimes things happen more through understanding and contact, than through words.
author: Sri M

text: What bars us from finding ‘That’ is too much knowledge, too much ego, too much feeling that ‘I know’. Nobody is ready to say ‘I don’t know’. In fact, in the present circumstances, there are more gurus than disciples. What to do? If one can at least say ‘I don’t know, let me find out’, that would be a very good thing.
author: Sri M

text: What is it that we seek? Why are we constantly seeking to better one thing after another? Because, we are hoping that ‘if I add something I might become happier’. But, we know, we can see in front of our eyes, that we keep on adding things and that happiness which we want to grasp seems to be elusive.
author: Sri M

text: Do your work to perfection. Don’t worry about what other people are evaluating.
author: Sri M

text: Instead of competition and wondering and wasting time on what happens if the other guy does better than me, fix your attention on what you are doing. It’ll turn out to be good.
author: Sri M

text: Can we live without depending on what others say? Who cares what others say. Let’s do what we have to do. Because otherwise you can’t move forward in this world.
author: Sri M

text: Yogi means one who can live in this world intelligently. A Karma Yogi is one who can navigate himself in this world where sometimes the currents are rough and sometimes they are smooth.
author: Sri M

text: The Yogi is able to navigate because he has an anchor which he can drop when he wants and pull it out when he wants. The art of actually negotiating life is Karma Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: The word yogi can be substituted for an ideal human being. The perfect yogi is one who doesn’t live on this earth worrying about what others think about them. In fact for the Yogi, insult and praise are on the same footing.
author: Sri M

text: Praise and flattery can actually retard your progress while somebody who says ‘Hey! You are not doing it right’. It’s a good thing for you. Consider it as a teaching and don’t consider it as something negative.
author: Sri M

text: If you are with a genuine teacher, even if you don’t speak and there are no words exchanged. It’s possible that you’ll get something if your minds are in close contact, not only physical. It’s usually misinterpreted as the physical, but it’s actually the minds.
author: Sri M

text: If the frequency of your mind and the frequency of my mind are at the same level, the wavelengths are same, then it’s possible without uttering a single word, something might pass. Not so much physical.
author: Sri M

text: The idea is to keep your mind in rapport with the teacher. However what one should remember is that the mind is more important than the body.
author: Sri M

text: The danger is when a person’s mind is settled down and he or she has a lot of energy inside, usually soothing energy, since the world is always looking for something soothing, there is a possibility that it may attract people. And the danger is to make that person’s physical presence more important than what he or she is trying to say.
author: Sri M

text: On the one hand there is this traditional thing of serving the teacher and being around. But I always keep reminding them that this is not so important. The most important thing is to listen to what I am trying to say and try to figure it out for yourself.
author: Sri M

text: The most difficult thing about life, is that it is so difficult to say ‘I don’t know’. Unfortunately everybody knows now-a-days and there are more number of gurus than disciples now.
author: Sri M

text: Turiya seems to be the basis on which waking, dream and deep sleep play around. Turiya is the original background.
author: Sri M

text: Suppose, in deep sleep, in the heavenly state of bliss, the mind wakes up as a witness and sees it. Normally it doesn’t. It remembers when you wake up. Suppose there is awareness of deep sleep. Then this becomes Turiya. Unfortunately you cannot define Turiya by deep sleep.
author: Sri M

text: The recognition of Turiya is Self-recognition. It’s not as if a third party is recognized. In the state called Turiya, Turiya itself is the witness of itself. There is no other entity out there to recognize it. This is our experience. This is what the acharyas also discussed.
author: Sri M

text: If you really want to have an anubhava (experience) of that Turiya, This little ‘I’, which says I am so and so, I am this, I know this, I don’t know this, I studied this, which also has attractions and is repulsed, it’s opposite views on various factors, when this ‘I’ has disappeared, then only That is there.
author: Sri M

text: If this little ‘I’, when it completely disappears when it becomes the ‘I’ of the little child, then you’ll know what is ‘Turiya’. When we reach close to it, ‘you’ are not there anymore. There is only Turiya. But it is conscious. It is not unconscious like deep sleep.
author: Sri M

text: Kashi is called the city of light. To see the light, first we need to decondition ourselves, free from all the preconceived ideas stuffed into us. Take it all out.
author: Sri M

text: The whole process of sublimating the lower to the higher is the meaning of ‘Shivaratri’. To free oneself from temptation, to be totally attached to the highest so when you touch that there is no more attachment left; until that happens we are in misery because our object of affection is a physical thing.
author: Sri M

text: Shiva is a perfect example, perfect representation of a yogi. Which of the Gods sits cross legged with eyes closed but Shiva. So that meditative posture in which these two eyes are closed, which means for the time being the external contact is suspended and the inner eye is opened.
author: Sri M

text: The best thing would be to move forward in spiritual training or sadhana till we are in a position to see if we are something other than the body. If we are other than the body, then surely somewhere ‘I’ must be even when the body is dead. It cannot suddenly wind up, what happens to all the energy that is there?
author: Sri M

text: If you advance in your sadhana, you will come to a point where you will actually know that you are not this body.
author: Sri M

text: The Gita says it beautifully saying, when the soul leaves the body and goes off carrying the seeds of it’s karmas like the wind carrying the fragrance of the flowers, you can’t see it, but it is there.
author: Sri M

text: Whatever potentialities that you have, whatever karmas that you performed, whatever likes and dislikes you have, most people don’t end their likes and dislikes by the time they die. It’s still there so you carry all of this and go away.
author: Sri M

text: The ‘sukshma sharira’ - subtle body is much more beautiful, finer than the ‘sthula sharira’, gross body which you have.
author: Sri M

text: What is the mind? The mind is made up of the movement of thought waves. You cannot conceive a mind without thought.
author: Sri M

text: Who is managing the mind? The mind itself is managing the mind. There’s no external entity managing it over there.
author: Sri M

text: If we think of a state of mind which is so quiet where there is no conflict, no distraction which is the aim of yoga, then you see there is something which is beyond the ordinary mind.
author: Sri M

text: Mindfulness is to watch your mind, be mindful of your mind while you are in the outside world, relating to others, reacting to what others say. It is to understand your mind as it is, not what you are going to make it into.
author: Sri M

text: Having gone through this for many years, having seen my mind and its layers and different potentialities for many years, I would say that the mind has infinite potential, it is not finite. For that you need to keep it free of conflict and distraction.
author: Sri M

text: Management is nothing to do with material, it is do with your minds. If you can do that, you can manage the world. If you can manage your mind, you can mind the other person’s mind provided there are no prejudices.
author: Sri M

text: The Bhagawat Gita, in my view is a classic text on not only in some way on managing the human mind but also on how to study the mind.
author: Sri M

text: The study of the mind is a very scientific one. It’s not something which is mumbo-jumbo. We have the instrument to do that and that is the ancient science of Yoga and the ancient science of Vedanta which studies the structure.
author: Sri M

text: Questions never end. When you figure out that questions are part of the movement of the mind, and everything is still, there is nothing left to ask. This is something that has to happen on its own; it’s not something that can be imposed on anybody.
author: Sri M

text: The idea of looking within is to close one's eyes, look into the mind, and see how it's functioning. There are hundreds of thoughts in there. Can I keep observing them with the belief that, one day, I want these thoughts to cease? Then, there's a chance that I would get in touch with the core of my being.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is not a passive state. It is a super-active state wherein there's action in the tranquility of mind, without agitation.
author: Sri M

text: Moderation in all areas - eating, drinking, sleeping, and also entertainment. It takes your mind off it’s constant work. But don’t make entertainment your sole aim in life.
author: Sri M

text: One of the biggest problems we face when we sit down to meditate is distraction. If we don’t fix a daily schedule, success is not possible. The mind, out of habit, runs in various directions; you should be able to catch and fix it.
author: Sri M

text: What we cannot explain, we call a miracle. Usually, miracles happen due to laws of nature that most people don’t know of. All the Yogi does is to tap these laws, so that he/she can operate it.
author: Sri M

text: All meditations essentially boil down to how to make the mind free of distractions, how to make it settle down, and finally how to remain in the eye of the storm, be completely free and not be distracted by anything.
author: Sri M

text: All human beings are constantly searching for something, name, fame, position, wealth, everything. And this search goes on and on till we die. My Guru Maheshwarnath Babaji, used to tell me that RIP is not necessarily ‘rest in peace’. He said it could be ‘Rise if Possible.’
author: Sri M

text: Until the mind is at rest, there cannot be peace
author: Sri M

text: If you need peace and tranquility and ultimate happiness, what you need to find is the source of it inside us, in our hearts - the core of our being.
author: Sri M

text: In the Rig Veda, there is a saying, ekam sat vipra bahudha vadanti - there is only one Truth but the wise call it by different names.
author: Sri M

text: The whole process of sadhana is to go within and touch the spark in us - core of our consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: All the sadhana we do is basically to clear our mind and allow the inner to come forth, to shine forth and the way we live.
author: Sri M

text: Bhakti, Devotion is a great way of looking at and finding the Truth, because in devotion you expect nothing but to have an experience of God.
author: Sri M

text: So a yogi or a saint or a holy man, is somebody who has eyes, who can see, and for them they see that the whole is much bigger than any definitions we have.
author: Sri M

text: One of the Upanishads says - yadvachan abhyuditam – that which words cannot describe, that is the true reality. The good news is that it’s also our inner core. It’s not far away that you cannot see it.
author: Sri M

text: Upanishad says - taddure tadvantike – it’s far and it’s so near. It’s far because we think, ‘Oh, it’s so vast’. It’s near, because it is our own essential being.
author: Sri M

text: According to the Pistis Sophia every human has to be crucified. It’s a symbolic gesture which means every human has to crucify his base instincts on the cross and the greatest crucifixion is the cutting of the ego into two. And then there is only divinity remaining, Sophia - the philosophy and the understanding of reality.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishad says that words cannot express the Truth, no language can and no words can describe it. In absolute silence when there is no formation of words, which means no formation of thought then perhaps something happens.
author: Sri M

text: Most intelligent people quickly discover the limitations of the intellect. Then one says now this is not going to work so what can I do? Then some other faculty opens up and that is intuition, true intuition.
author: Sri M

text: True intuition - you can call it the opening of the single eye, not physically. The opening, the separating of the curtains comes only when you surrender after understanding that whatever circus you do with your ordinary mind, you cannot touch it. Then the other opens up. That is the intuition towards the Divine.
author: Sri M

text: There are many kinds of well-being - physical, mind, and spirit. The only shortcut to spiritual well-being is not an easy one - Cut the ego into two.
author: Sri M

text: The Self includes everyone. Not a single person or a being can be excluded from the big Self when one embraces IT.
author: Sri M

text: Once you touch it, even a little bit, even if you touch the hem of garment of Truth, then there is no more fear, there is no more anxiety, there is no more confusion in the mind.
author: Sri M

text: If you are physically fine and your mind is always agitated, you cannot call it well-being. On the other hand, if your mind is settled in well-being, even if you are not physically so OK, nothing matters because you are free.
author: Sri M

text: The condition of the mind is reflected in the condition of the body, and it also happens the other way around.
author: Sri M

text: People think, Oh! All this philosophy kind of kills you, No!. You are giving up small trinkets to actually touch the treasure which is in us.
author: Sri M

text: When one forgets one’s limitations and gets fully absorbed in the spirit of the Lord - this is Bhakti Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: In sleep you forget everything. There is no recognition outside or inside. There is complete quietness and yet there seems to be some witness enjoying because when we wake up we always say, Oh! I had a blissful sleep. So, there also is a witness.
author: Sri M

text: When you are dreaming, the dream is very real. When you wake up, it’s an illusion, it doesn’t exist. So, that which exists in one state of consciousness and does not exist in another, can you call it reality, the Sat ? There is only One Reality - the witness.
author: Sri M

text: There is a consciousness which witnesses everything. And if this consciousness due to applying your mind and due to your practices, can become the witness even when you are in deep sleep, then you are free.
author: Sri M

text: We should have food. We should have a place to stay, but you cannot find happiness by increasing your holdings.
author: Sri M

text: Let go and rejoice does not mean give up and rejoice. Letting go is different from giving up. Can we live in this world without carrying the unpleasant memories of our past experiences? Can we let go of that?
author: Sri M

text: The essence of happiness, the spark of the Divine is in the heart. When that is understood, you get some sense of what the Divine is. And for that you need to have some control over your emotions, your thoughts, the way you look at people, and be free of obsessions of what happened yesterday. Free yourself from it.
author: Sri M

text: The treasure shines in our hearts. We just need to turn around and look in. That’s called the ‘nivritti marg’. When that happens, then you have Supreme well-being.
author: Sri M

text: Non-violence, Ahimsa is not just non-killing, but also not having a grudge against anybody.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is beyond asanas, and that is true well-being.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is getting rid of all the distractions of the mind. When all the distractions of the mind are gone, then it becomes beautiful like a pond which has no ripples and in that you can see the reflection of your true Self.
author: Sri M

text: To practice Yoga and to make your mind quiet, calm and without ripples, you should live a life of moderation. Don’t go to extremes. If you completely don’t eat food, you can’t meditate. And if you eat too much food, instead of Samadhi you get into Sushupti . So, moderation is essential in food, work, exercise and entertainment.
author: Sri M

text: Treat all human beings the same way, no matter how they dress, how they are. Spend some time meditating on your Inner Self and little by little one day you will touch the source of well -being which fortunately for us is not anywhere outside but is inside our hearts.
author: Sri M

text: If your mood is reflected in the pattern of your breathing, can we turn it around and adjust the pattern of our breathing so that our moods are altered? From this came the entire science of Pranayama.
author: Sri M

text: Pratyahara is the capacity, developed through practice, by which you can shift your mind from one thing to another at short notice.
author: Sri M

text: Dharana is to develop the capacity of one-pointed attention. When the Dharana continues for some time without interruption, then it automatically becomes Dhyana or meditation.
author: Sri M

text: If you begin in earnest, then you will surely find well-being. The Ultimate well being is when the mind is quiet and calm and is resting on the Supreme Being whose very essence is Sat-Chit-Ananda, whose very essence is happiness.
author: Sri M

text: Once your mind is fully absorbed, where even you don’t exist except That, there is no better well being than That. And that well-being reflects itself in daily activities, in our behaviour.
author: Sri M

text: If you have touched the source of the fountain, you’ve touched the foundation of joy, does it matter if somebody is ignoring you or saying that you are a fool? So what!
author: Sri M

text: ‘Ishq’ means the ecstasy or ‘lahiri’ induced in the hearts of the devotees and the Yogis. Real Ishq is enjoying ecstasy, the lahiri of being completely one with the Inner Being which is a spark of the all-pervading Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: Once someone has drunk the wine of ‘fanaa’, not complete annihilation, but the annihilation of the ego, the small self, then only the big Self is visible to us.
author: Sri M

text: Sleep is when we are back to our original essence. The inner ‘me’ is there. You’ll say, ‘But I’m not aware of it.’ There we have shed everything, all individuality and we are what we actually are, which is a blissful non-corporeal being. This is what we are.
author: Sri M

text: We think that we are in charge of everything that is happening in this world yet we are not even in charge of anything that is happening in our body.
author: Sri M

text: Understand yourself. Everything that you need is in you. There is nothing outside. Be independent and wherever possible, be kind to others.
author: Sri M

text: If Shiva doesn’t do his ‘Tandava nritya’, then the images, shapes, and forms will not shatter and you will never see the reality behind them.
author: Sri M

text: The sacredness, the happiness, the vastness that you seek, the solution for the 'never-ending desires' that you seek sometimes, all this is just there with you, in you.
author: Sri M

text: In alone-ness, there is all happiness, there is no need to depend on anybody
author: Sri M

text: While it is a good thing to cultivate positive thoughts and to keep negative thoughts at bay, from the pure point of spiritual understanding, there is no positive or negative thought. It is all thought. The freer you are from it, the better. Thought itself is corrupt.
author: Sri M

text: tena tyaktena bhunjitha' Some people have translated as 'give up and rejoice' but I like to translate it as 'let go and rejoice'.
author: Sri M

text: You are a spark of the Supreme Being! All the happiness and sorrow, and everything that happens, is pervaded by that Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: Let go' does not mean you should throw everything away and go to the forest. It means - develop the quality of 'letting go'. Then there is absolute peace - and rejoice!
author: Sri M

text: One of the aspects of ‘let go and rejoice’ is allowing the action to mentally let go if it’s present now.
author: Sri M

text: The only way to get rid of negativity is to bring in positivity. You can't remove negativity by constantly thinking about it. You need to replace it with positive thinking.
author: Sri M

text: Miracles can happen only if you can change the attitude of your mind and implement your resolutions.
author: Sri M

text: Spirituality basically means that the human being realizes his mundane world’s limitations and reaches out to see if there is something which is unlimited, unconditional, and infinite.
author: Sri M

text: Be truthful, do not cause pain to others, be simple, do good to others, and most importantly, strive to attain closeness to the Supreme Being,
author: Sri M

text: If you are deeply spiritual and if you are into spiritual practice and you follow the ground rules of spiritual practice, then one need not profess to formally belong to a particular religion.
author: Sri M

text: You can be religious and at the same time be spiritual. There need not be a dichotomy, you can be both, or you can be anyone.
author: Sri M

text: To be religious only and not spiritual, is just to follow the outwards form of religion, which means you are just following the shell and not going to the essence.
author: Sri M

text: Every religion has a core, which is spiritual and if you are merely following the formalities and not going to the core, then you are really not practicing the religion
author: Sri M

text: Sadhana is not about doing something and reaching somewhere; one purifies the vessel to be fit to receive the full flow of the grace of knowledge.
author: Sri M

text: Sadhana is meant to go deep into the realities, into the truth of the Upanishads, into the core of the teachings, into the core of one's being.
author: Sri M

text: Upanishad: upa means to move closer, and shad means to settle down, sit, relax, listen. The in-between word ni indicates the connection between going near and sitting down.
author: Sri M

text: Gayatri Mantra, the most important prayer of the Rigveda says ‘illumine my intellect’. Sharpen the mind so that it can understand its limitations.
author: Sri M

text: Bhakti is the deep feeling in the heart; of devotion to the truth, if you are interested in some form of God, which you worship. Attachment to that itself is bhakti.
author: Sri M

text: Two times are very important for any kind of spiritual practice: one is dawn and the other is dusk. Both are called Sandhya because they are the coming together of the two lights - darkness and light.
author: Sri M

text: If the mind is to be shaken up from its beliefs, and from its sleep of ignorance, then it has to be woken up from the stupor in which it is caught.
author: Sri M

text: Humility means the understanding or the awareness that one doesn’t know or perhaps, there is more to know. This means the idea that one ‘knows’ has to be set aside, that the brain or mind is empty to receive and not congested with stuff.
author: Sri M

text: The mind has to be shaken up from wrong ideas; essentially meaning, a churning-up - ‘ manthan ’ is required. It’s only when the mind is churned-up that it can explore fresh horizons; otherwise, it becomes fossilized.
author: Sri M

text: The word Guru means heavy, in Sanskrit. It also means teacher. Heavy – meaning one who is more important, who has more understanding; who has more than you have; who, by virtue of his knowledge, is a heavyweight. That’s the meaning of the word
author: Sri M

text: Observe the children without prejudice. Don't try to put them into the moulds that you want to put them. They may fit into it, but deep down there is no happiness. A rose is a rose and a lotus is a lotus. They should be allowed to bloom in their own essence.
author: Sri M

text: We like to be happy, we gather things. Somewhere along the line, we have been taught that the more you gather, the more happy you are. Not really true.
author: Sri M

text: That happiness and fulfillment, which the Vedas describe as Poornamadah poornamidam poornaat poornamudachyate; is there in the depth of one's core consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: The inner being is defined by the Upanishads as our own inner essence, Atma, a spark of the Supreme, which is called the Parabrahman or the Paramatma.
author: Sri M

text: Everybody is seeking God for the truth, in different ways, thinking it is somewhere else. One has to just reverse and look within.
author: Sri M

text: Liberation means not to be bound by anything. The greatest bondage is our own mind not outward things.
author: Sri M

text: The God who sits in our hearts, the antaryami, is truth, consciousness, and bliss. The whole attempt in the spiritual journey is to find this.
author: Sri M

text: The greatest of bhaktas is the one who keeps the welfare of all the living beings in his heart, sarva-bhuta-hite-ratah.
author: Sri M

text: Sādhanā is all about the search within; it is a journey from extroversion to introversion.
author: Sri M

text: Sādhanā doesn’t mean that the Sādhak neglects the world. One has to only turn inwards in order to find the truth, which is one’s own self.
author: Sri M

text: The search for one’s true identity and happiness is not just reserved for monks or sanyasis. Every human being, without distinction, can embark upon this search.
author: Sri M

text: To do Sādhanā, one has to find an appropriate time to sit in solitude and practice. Once one becomes an expert at this, Sādhanā can be done anywhere in the world.
author: Sri M

text: The practice of Sādhanā is merely a method passed onto a student by a spiritual teacher, who has practiced it himself and is customized for the student before transmitting it.
author: Sri M

text: In the Vedas, the subjective experience of the true self is defined as Sat-cit-ānanda. Sat meaning truth, Cit meaning consciousness, and Ananda meaning happiness.
author: Sri M

text: If one is fulfilled, happy within oneself, independent of anything external, and still exudes happiness, then there is no necessity to do Sādhanā.
author: Sri M

text: The search for happiness is effective, only when the mind begins to change. This comes from Sādhanā, which is much more than sitting down in a quiet place and keeping one’s eyes closed.
author: Sri M

text: There is more to Sādhanā than merely sitting, closing one’s eyes, and pretending to meditate. It has to be complemented by one’s activity in the world; how one deals with other human beings.
author: Sri M

text: The true Sādhakā does not limit oneself to meditating in the way the Guru advises but also begins to understand that this divine spark in oneself is also in other living beings.
author: Sri M

text: Kindness and doing good should go hand-in-hand with one’s meditative practices. They complement each other, resulting in one’s spiritual growth.
author: Sri M

text: You are not sheep that can be herded together and made to eat the same food. Spiritual development is an individual affair.
author: Sri M

text: Many people think that Yoga is distinct from Vedanta - as a philosophical system, it is. But, in practice, they are very close to each other because they are different paths to the same goal.
author: Sri M

text: If you have an Ishta Devata or you worship a great saint whom you consider as God incarnate, it is at that point that you can visualize him sitting in your heart and becoming one with you - this is called Guru Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: If we center our attention to our hearts and bow down to all living beings, and since every living being is a temple, we are moving along the path of yoga.
author: Sri M

text: The practice of yoga is the way of finding that happiness, which is our true identity; when we discover that we are not what we think we are, but something completely different.
author: Sri M

text: A yogi in any situation has inner peace. That yogi is the best who discovers his own self and feels the same Self resides in all.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is not for one who eats too much or eats too little, or sleeps too much or sleeps too little. Which means there has to be moderation somewhere; a middle path has to be followed.
author: Sri M

text: A yogi is a person who has full control over his mind and senses, so at a given point he would be able to switch onto something or switch off from something. Practicing this is called pratyahara.
author: Sri M

text: The best way to calm the breath and therefore calm the mind automatically is - not by controlling it, but by watching it, mentally. So, this is a simple exercise - no secrets!
author: Sri M

text: The most important application of asanas in meditation is " sthira sukham asana "; that means the posture in which you can sit for a length of time in sukha , without fidgeting, without pain, comfortably; that is your asana for meditation.
author: Sri M

text: Perfect health consists of physical and mental well-being permeated by a sense of sacredness. Everything around us, from a speck of dust to the tallest mountain and the roaring oceans, are sacred. When this dimension of sacredness is added to the definition of health, the concept of health becomes multi-dimensional.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga asanas with the help of pranayama, help to activate certain centers along the spine. In yoga, these are called chakras where the cosmic energy enters the system.
author: Sri M

text: In the yogic anatomy, the sushumna nadi is described as the central channel through which the energies have to move in order to awaken a person to the higher reality.
author: Sri M

text: Meditation is also a churning of the mind. When the Samudra Manthan is done, the first thing that comes out is the poison. Amrita only comes last.
author: Sri M

text: The thought that 'I must change' is the beginning of dharana and the steps that you take towards it is the practice of yoga. The result of doing the yoga is the dhyana and the ultimate result of dhyana is Samadhi.
author: Sri M

text: Samadhi is the gateway for the mind to enter greater levels of consciousness and be free of all conditioning, the state of This is the final aim of all Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: Bhakti Yoga with regular practice of Japa and meditation can help the mind become one-pointed and silent.
author: Sri M

text: Pranayama is the science of life, and prana when it is only the breath is called the shvasa. Shvasa and prana are interlinked. And therefore, if you keep your shvasa under certain conditions, your prana gets activated.
author: Sri M

text: As the yogi meditates and as his levels of consciousness rises from the gross to the subtle, touching each center on his spinal cord, which are known as Chakras, his consciousness ascends from the consciousness of mundane things to higher and higher levels until finally, it reaches the level of the multi-dimensional supreme reality.
author: Sri M

text: A healthy body is required for Sadhana, which is why basically we do asanas, pranayama, mudras, and so on.
author: Sri M

text: The word Guru is made of two syllables 'gu' and 'ru'. ‘Gu’ means that which is hidden or which is not exposed and 'ru' is the short form of Rudra who is the destroyer of darkness or bondage or ignorance. So the Guru is one who leads you to the light, or who destroys ignorance and clears the cobwebs.
author: Sri M

text: A Guru cannot be known by the clothes he wears, or the rosary he wears around his neck, the drama which surrounds him, or by the number of disciples he has. A genuine spiritual teacher, cannot be recognized by the external paraphernalia.
author: Sri M

text: A true Guru is always ready to help you move forward in your spiritual journey so that you may ultimately drink the real nectar of immortality and absolute bliss which he is ready to give you.
author: Sri M

text: A genuine spiritual teacher as far as possible does not exhibit his powers simply for the reason that a genuine seeker is not interested in his powers, miracles, protection, or anything of this kind.
author: Sri M

text: The true spiritual teacher is like a highly polished mirror which, held before your face, shows exactly who and what you are, the content of your mind, what flatterers say you are, and what you actually are not.
author: Sri M

text: A true teacher is one who will tell you what steps to take to reach the goal. Will hold your hand and help you walk the path. He or she will not fall for flattery; he or she will not eye your wealth.
author: Sri M

text: One of the main functions of the Guru is to make you stand on your own feet. A true Guru does not want you to be dependent on anybody. He wants you to flower and ultimately become free. His objective is freedom for you and not to bind you even to himself.
author: Sri M

text: The relationship with the Guru should be like a friendship. The teacher has a lot of responsibility once he accepts a student. But I think even the student should think for himself or herself with all the freedom that the teacher has given. Once decided, take the responsibility of being a good student. That’s why this relationship is individual. It is not a mass relationship.
author: Sri M

text: The only thing the Guru is genuinely concerned with is your spiritual progress. The moment you are serious, so serious that nothing else is more important to you than finding the truth; your Guru will come to you.
author: Sri M

text: Mindfulness is to watch your mind, be mindful of it while you are in the outside world, relating to others, and reacting to what others say. It is to understand your mind as it is, not what it is to be made into.
author: Sri M

text: Freedom is like the Wheel of Enlightenment – the rim symbolizes mindfulness while the hub stands for moral discipline. The veil of illusion is gradually lifted as one goes deeper into understanding one’s own mind.
author: Sri M

text: The experience of spiritual perfection – when it happens, is something which needs no other proof; it is in itself a proof.
author: Sri M

text: The ultimate happiness that we all seek, lies in finding one’s true self. And when we find that, the heart becomes very soft, kind and understanding
author: Sri M

text: OM represents the whole creation, universe, cosmos, human being, the connection between a human and the universe, the connection between the individual and the Supreme all-pervading being.
author: Sri M

text: When you meet people every day, try to look at them and your relationship with them as something new, don’t carry the old with you. This is also a way to overcome the limitations of one’s own mind.
author: Sri M

text: Many things that we see in the world through our five senses actually limit the unlimited and give us a very conditioned and limited picture.
author: Sri M

text: A belief that perhaps there is something greater, the world cannot be just this limited and conditioned thing that I see with my eyes - That is the beginning of expanding to newer horizons, higher dimensions, and greater consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: One of the ways of transcending the ordinary mind and understanding that All-pervading consciousness is through silencing the noisy mind, which chatters from the time we are born till the time we die.

text: Peace is a state of mind that comes from inside, if I am not peaceful with myself I cannot be at peace anywhere.
author: Sri M

text: If you can be mindful of your thoughts, of your actions, of your meditation, of your breath, and so on, that is called mindfulness – a total mindfulness as you go along with life.
author: Sri M

text: ‘Sangachchadhwam, samvadadhwam samvo manamsi janatam’ which means may we walk together, may we study together with our minds put together, may we understand.
author: Sri M

text: It’s only in this world when you meet somebody, when you talk to people, how you behave, what you do that you figure out where you are, otherwise you can’t figure out, you cannot figure this out in isolation, because there is no reaction.
author: Sri M

text: To look at yourself first to find out how you are in the midst of circumstances, I think is the beginning of knowing yourself.
author: Sri M

text: That infinite consciousness which we're trying to explore and that is nowhere to be sought except in oneself because that’s one's true Id and not the body or the mind or any of those other things.
author: Sri M

text: Even if you don't have belief in a kind of a Supreme God, especially the thundering variety, you can still progress in yoga and find the essence of consciousness
author: Sri M

text: Ultimately, you are your own master. There is no other one. A teacher can help you understand that you are your own teacher. If you understand that then you are free.
author: Sri M

text: If you need to go deeper into your mind and understand the essence of your consciousness, then your mindfulness should be all the time.
author: Sri M

text: Ishavasyam idam sarvam – that Supreme Being pervades everything here. Yat kincha jagatyam jagat – that which moves and that which does not move. Tena tyaktena bhunjitha – therefore, give up and rejoice!
author: Sri M

text: Knowing yourself starts with knowing myself, in the midst of other people, not alone
author: Sri M

text: There are ways to get in touch with the essence of your being - consciousness. It is beyond all religions and philosophies. Once you begin to see the possibility of getting to the core of your consciousness, then you can no longer be the same person.
author: Sri M

text: What you seek spiritually is right there inside you and we search for it everywhere. It is in us, in our hearts, there is a beautiful treasure which we always miss.
author: Sri M

text: The simile of the lotus that grows in and derives its nourishment from water and yet doesn’t let water wet its petals. Water can’t stay on the petals of the lotus; it rolls off as droplets. That’s the kind of life that a yogi lives.
author: Sri M

text: How do we know about the spiritual stature of a person, how? We can’t measure it, you need to be with the person for some time to figure out what he is like and a true spiritual teacher will rarely advertise.
author: Sri M

text: Go on meditating deeper and deeper until the mind is stripped bare and you find your own dear ‘Self’, the radiant, unpolluted, indestructible, pure consciousness, the unalloyed bliss.
author: Sri M

text: Absorb yourself in devotional music and let it carry you to higher states of consciousness. Once you taste the wine of devotion, you’ll never want to touch lesser intoxicants.
author: Sri M

text: All great things have been achieved by asking and questioning, not otherwise!
author: Sri M

text: One of the most important changes that take place in one’s spiritual evolution, is kindness and compassion that fill the heart. Unless and Until the heart becomes kind, one doesn’t become perfect in the spiritual field.

text: This Self which is the basic consciousness behind every individual, has, according to Vedanta, no differentiations such as this and that or you and me.

text: Pranayama plays a major role to keep the body supplied with the right quantity of oxygen, and at the same time calming the mind and helping it turn inward into tranquil meditation status.

text: When a spiritual teacher says something, it’s not the words that are important, but the effect it has on you.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind and the senses have ceased to function externally, in that tranquility and absolute stillness, you find what is actually there.
author: Sri M

text: If the mind or the flute is emptied of all dross, all pretensions, prejudices, greed, anger, everything out! You have to offer it clean, only then, Krishna takes the flute and plays.
author: Sri M

text: The key to clear thinking and problem solving is an alert and relaxed mind. Concentration is not tension. On the contrary, it is possible only when the mind is relaxed and attentive.
author: Sri M

text: If the Supreme Being is all-pervading Brahman and is also in our hearts as a spark, why do you worship? author: Sri M

text: Detachment is a natural process and it happens when you get attached to something higher. Then attachment to smaller things falls off.
author: Sri M

text: Freedom has so many concepts. If you really want to enjoy freedom, you should first figure out that you are bound. Many people are bound but think they are free. To understand the bondage, the chains with which we are bound is the first step to free oneself.
author: Sri M

text: A very major function of a true spiritual teacher is to act as a well-polished mirror so we see where the mistakes are, and where we miss seeing certain important factors.
author: Sri M

text: To find out what is true, the mind must be free. Free of rituals, of beliefs, of dogmas, knowledge, and experience. It is only then that the mind can realize that which is true because such a mind is quiet.
author: Sri M

text: All ‘this’ that you see is the Truth the only thing is, it is veiled. You remove the veil, and all differences disappear. Then ‘this’ becomes no different from ‘that Brahman .’ There is no differentiation between ‘this’ and ‘that’ because differentiation is caused by the dividing mind.
author: Sri M

text: Happiness is a state of mind not dependent on anything you possess.
author: Sri M

text: Human life is like the bubble that appears in the stream. You see it one moment and then, the next moment, it is gone.
author: Sri M

text: You are the consciousness, which is the witness of all the drama, watching in amusement as the ego plays its games and dons different masks at different times. The real you is that ever-blissful, unchanging, blessed consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: If your body is healthy, your mind is healthy. Your mind is healthy, you are getting ready for ascension to spiritual health, and then you go beyond. So this is the reason why yoga is practiced.
author: Sri M

text: The Guru principle, which means the principle by which one learns from the teacher, is forever. Now and then there are people coming, teaching, and going away. But that doesn't mean the teaching ever ends - it is always there.
author: Sri M

text: For a mind that is still, and in that stillness, there is an abundance of energy.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t ever get yourself discouraged by any circumstances. Move ahead and you will overcome it.
author: Sri M

text: Every failure is a stepping stone. When you fail, it’s a great opportunity given to see ‘why did I fail’.
author: Sri M

text: All methods of meditation and spiritual disciplines are meant to turn your mind within, make it tranquil, peaceful, and kinder. When you touch that joy which is within, you can lead a joyous life.
author: Sri M

text: The mind is always moving up and down. Sometimes here, sometimes there. Sometimes happy, sometimes sad. It is like a roller-coaster ride. Yoga is to balance this movement of the mind and make it quiet. Because for anything spiritual to happen and to go beyond the ordinary understanding, you need to have a tranquil mind.
author: Sri M

text: When you say Guru, it means a teacher in all ways; could be a small child who teaches you innocence of childhood, it could be a philosophical teacher who teaches you the Upanishads, they are all Gurus.
author: Sri M

text: If you don’t watch where you go in your outer life, if you don’t know what you are doing, and if you are not aware of your actions and reactions that you have on others in this world, then it’s almost futile to sit and look at mindfulness within.
author: Sri M

text: Whenever a Satya Kama—one who searches for nothing but the Truth, sits in humility before a teacher, with his mind unbiased and open, ready to receive what is given, the teaching or learning involved in such a process is considered the Upanishad, the Truth
author: Sri M

text: A human being should think of himself as part of this entire universe and not a separate isolated thing. This is a vast network and the consciousness is not confined to one center. It’s actually all-pervading, one Global consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: Who Am I? Where do I come from? Is this drama all that exists in this world or there is something more? When one wants to find out one’s true individuality, that’s one kind of approach to meditation
author: Sri M

text: Human mind is hypnotized into a trance-like state by beliefs, by situations, and by the attractions of the outside world. Waking up from it to make the mind multidimensional is the process of de-hypnotizing oneself.
author: Sri M

text: The most important service you can render to a spiritual teacher is to understand and follow the teachings. That’s the best way to give respect to the teacher.
author: Sri M

text: Krishna said to Arjuna in Gita that Karma Yoga is working effortlessly without even wondering what the fruits are. I think every human being can, to some extent, practice it and gradually become perfect.
author: Sri M

text: If you really practice outer and inner mindfulness and are able to look into your mind, then you can become more human than before.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishad says ‘letting go’ can be done only when it is understood that the Supreme Being pervades everything. The rejoicing is in the understanding that your very Self is not different from Isha, that Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: Once you are stabilized in your inner self, it becomes easier to function in this world. Because the mind is calm and doesn’t get agitated, it does what it has to, quietly.
author: Sri M

text: One who enjoys his own self in himself without depending on what others say or what happens in the outside world, such a person is called a man of steady wisdom.
author: Sri M

text: When one finds that true happiness is within and not outside, one gives more importance to the inner journey than the outer, then one finds satisfaction in oneself.
author: Sri M

text: We should be mindful of the outside world and how we interact with it and then mindful of what happens within. Both have to go together, which is why in yoga there are yama, niyama - rules and regulations to be followed in daily life.
author: Sri M

text: The ancient teachers said that there is a link between your breathing pattern and emotional states, and if you change the rhythm or pattern of your breath, you can change your emotional state. You can change your mood.
author: Sri M

text: When you become aware of your breathing under all circumstances, not just when you meditate, you will notice then, that your mind becomes settled and you go deeper into the inner layers. This is called awareness of breath, mindfulness, watchfulness.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishad says if you want to understand the Supreme Reality that pervades everywhere, you need to ‘let go’ and move away from your own ‘small’ center. Expand, let everyone be a part of you.
author: Sri M

text: If you are tranquil and peaceful in yourself then the peacefulness can be shared with others.
author: Sri M

text: All joys spring forth from within your being, the reservoir of all joy, the essence of all bliss in your heart, in the core of your own being.
author: Sri M

text: There are two parts of the spiritual journey, one is the life you lead following certain rules and regulations and the other is how to go within.
author: Sri M

text: According to Yoga Sutras of Patanjali ‘ Sthira Sukham Asanam’ that posture where you can effortlessly stay for a long time and in happiness, without pain, is considered to be the best asana for meditation.
author: Sri M

text: If the yearning is very deep in your heart that what you want to find is the truth and not powers, then I can assure you that you will come to the right teacher at the right time.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind is calm and quiet, aware of itself, when it is mindful of the outer and inner and also of the breath, then the divided mind slowly starts to integrate.
author: Sri M

text: If we have gone deep into the wisdom of the rishis and seen that the same Supreme Reality is everywhere, then you have no reason to treat anybody in a bad way. If you don't harm somebody, then you are in peace and your happiness is found
author: Sri M

text: Be mindful of your breathing. Understand how valuable it is to you, how nourishing it is to you. It is a link between you and your inner consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: If one has to be a 'stitha prajna'—that is, maintain the mind in a calm, quiet and tranquil in all circumstances, we have to ‘let go’ and move forward
author: Sri M

text: This ‘Self’ of yours is ever free, ever blissful. It is and was never bound, therefore, there is no question of making it free.
author: Sri M

text: If you cultivate a friendship with your breath, you will reach the essence from where the breath arises. Breath is the connection between the divine and the physical.
author: Sri M

text: The primary function of the teacher is to clean the mirror and show it at the right angle so that you see yourself as you actually are, not what you want to be
author: Sri M

text: We are always searching for happiness and feel we can find it outside. Turn the direction and you will find the treasure right inside you
author: Sri M

text: What is change, other than movement? The only changeless thing on earth is change. Everything else will change. Nothing is stable, nothing is steady, inside there is infinite movement going on.
author: Sri M

text: One can start with ten minutes of introspection daily and then slowly proceed to the more important and intricate aspects of meditation.
author: Sri M

text: What is important is to discover that the fulfillment and happiness, the poornata that you seek, is in the core of your consciousness and cannot be acquired elsewhere.

text: With ‘I know’ comes the ego, and as long as that ego remains, it is not possible to find one’s true essence.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is the stilling of the mind, the stopping of all the modifications of the mind, and freeing the mind from all its distractions. When it becomes absolutely quiet, that state is called ‘Kaivalya’.

text: On the path of spirituality, the journey is as important as the goal.
author: Sri M

text: Upanishad says, when you find the truth, you find it’s That one Truth which pervades everything. It’s complete, it doesn’t diminish, it’s always there. And the good news is, we are also a part of That.

text: One of the most important markers of spiritual progress is how soft our heart is, whether we feel the pain of others, our care for others, not just our family but others.

text: Observing oneself in a relationship with others is a very important part of spiritual sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: Deep down somewhere in the core of our consciousness, there is this understanding, which we don’t see, that I am actually complete and I have to get back to that completeness.

text: The teaching of Vedanta is that this happiness that one is seeking is not anywhere in the outside world. What we need to find is that in the middle of our activities, there is a permanent sense of happiness, within us. This is our true essential nature.

text: Be mindful of your breathing. Understand how valuable it is to you, how nourishing it is to you. It is a link between you and your inner being.
author: Sri M

text: Meditation is usually done to keep the mind tranquil, If it only works when you sit down, it’s a good thing, but if it also works when you are in this tumultuous world, then it is even better.

text: If you have happiness as your aim, get ready to sacrifice everything else for it. Happiness is not attainable by acquiring and gathering. It is reached by being good and 'letting go!

text: That Absolute energy, in manifestation or movement, when it begins to work, is called Shakti. When it is in its potential form, absolutely at rest, without a single movement – That completeness is Shiva, the Absolute Being.

text: Energy – once its work of creation, preservation, and destruction is done – still remains whole. The whole Cosmos is spun out of this energy or Shakti, which keeps working tirelessly and yet remains unaltered.

text: When the third eye or the agna chakra is activated and the kundalini energy reaches the agna , the mind understands the reality behind all illusion. Then all illusions are burnt to ashes and this is the last but one step towards Moksha .

text: I can physically run away from my situation but I can’t run away from my mind as the mind follows me, wherever I go. So stay where you are and deal with the situation.

author: Sri M

text: As your feelings become more and more subtle, deeper centers of the human mind open up to form a link to that which is beyond the ordinary mind.
author: Sri M

text: Shraddha has several meanings but one of the meanings is complete attention - total one-pointed attention.
author: Sri M

text: True consciousness means to go beyond all images. Not images that you see around you but the images that we build up in our minds. It is because of these images that we get hurt, our ego goes up and we have all the problems.
author: Sri M

text: Do your duties but don’t neglect your spiritual journey. Keep up your duties seriously, so that when you are mature enough, you are out of it.
author: Sri M

text: Sit down and meditate in your heart center and whenever such thoughts come which are not related to the inner, try to keep them away.
author: Sri M

text: Our entire life is sadhana – how we approach it, how we manage it, how we are moving towards our goal – this is sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: If one understands that one is not the body but the inner self which is consciousness, then one begins to understand how to deal with sorrow.
author: Sri M

text: When we are infants, we are helpless... We can’t eat, somebody has to feed us. During the end too, when we become old, helpless, and fall sick, again the same thing happens. In between, there is a period, when we really think or imagine that we are under control. Actually, we are not. If we realize this, then we have surrendered.
author: Sri M

text: Freedom is our birthright. Our true self, the atman is free; it does not need to be freed from anything. It is free because it is complete, ‘ purna ’. ‘ Purnamadah ’ - That completeness is actually ‘you’ in your true essence.
author: Sri M

text: When the limited understands its limitations; that is intelligence.
author: Sri M

text: Break free from all bondage, all psychological bondage, realize that your true self is ever free and never bound!
author: Sri M

text: Reality is not that things don’t exist but may not be in the form or state in which we think they do. That wrong understanding of objects, of anything is called Maya , a misunderstanding. And that is the great illusion.
author: Sri M

text: If you have faith in an infinite Supreme Being, put all your heart into what you want to do or achieve.
author: Sri M

text: The yogic theory is that the source of all enjoyment, the reservoir of all happiness is within us, the spark of the divine called Sat-Chit-Ananda.
author: Sri M

text: Once you learn the art of being one-pointed in meditation or in day to day life, you are automatically in a meditative state all the time.
author: Sri M

text: Let’s say the guide, the teacher, or friend who has crossed to the other side, who has learnt to swim and cross the ocean of samsara , such a teacher who is our true friend, what does he do? He teaches you how to swim so that you can cross the ocean.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind is open, and when there is a great desire to achieve something then the channels for achieving it are opened.
author: Sri M

text: In matters beyond the rational mind, realization takes place only when this mind becomes absolutely still. To find that out, we need a rational mind!
author: Sri M

text: All things about spiritual matters boil down to your relationships, day to day. We can sit at home and meditate for hours but when we come out and we are still the same, it does not work.
author: Sri M

text: If we can voluntarily extricate ourselves from the conditioning thoughts that are in our minds and open up for receiving what is beyond the three-dimensional world and the ordinary way of thinking, perhaps we can tap the infinite potential that is even now, waiting for us inside our own minds.
author: Sri M

text: Remove all the conditions that are there and remain in that One essential state.
author: Sri M

text: You have a slate and you write on it. Every time you write on it, if you want to write anything else, you have to rub it off. So in matters of inner exploration, the most important thing is to keep your slate clean.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t unnecessarily complicate life with too many things. That does not mean that when you speak the truth you have to be blunt. There are sweet ways of speaking the truth.
author: Sri M

text: When we say control your thoughts during meditation, it is impossible to do that and make them disappear. Because the moment you try to make thoughts disappear, you are ‘thinking’.
author: Sri M

text: A Kshatriya is a person who has won over his animal instincts – he is called the greatest conqueror.
author: Sri M

text: The Supreme Being is the connecting link between all beings, worlds, and galaxies, passing through them all like a thread holding the beads together in a rosary.
author: Sri M

text: If all my mind is concentrated on seeking the Truth, then I am what in the Upanishads is called Satya Kama. That means I have no kaama other than seeking satya.
author: Sri M

text: Very often, we tend to mistake tamas – Tamo guna – for sattva . Sattva is goodness and calmness and quietness. Tamo guna is not goodness and calmness and quietness but laziness, sloth, and pretending to be good.
author: Sri M

text: Does freedom happen in stages? I would say, It’s like the wheel; the network of illusion is gradually lifted as one goes deeper and deeper into understanding one’s own self, one’s own mind.
author: Sri M

text: Moving up and down the spine is Mukhya Prana , the Supreme energy. In yogic terms, it is the movement of the aspiration, thought, concentration and energy towards the higher side or the lower side. When it descends, it leads to material well-being. When it ascends, it leads to Spiritual well-being
author: Sri M

text: The more something is done only for oneself, I can say it is wrong. The more something is done for others and of that a little bit is for oneself, then I can say it is the right way. That is the only distinction I can make between right and wrong.
author: Sri M

text: Great yogis, great rishis, great scientists, the ‘great’ in all fields, are those who are not satisfied believing the conditioned mind. They know that this is a prejudice and try hard to break through, come out of their shells and soar to great heights.
author: Sri M

text: When you enter the meditation hall, leave your ego outside along with your shoes; don’t bring it in. Go inside like a new-born child who is free - you have no enemies, you don’t hate anybody, at least for the time being.
author: Sri M

text: In any martial art like Kalaripayattu they say, ‘never do anything when you are angry’ because all your calculations may go wrong. So let your anger go, cool down, and then perform the action.
author: Sri M

text: The rishis –seeing how people are constantly unhappy; seeking all the time and not getting the ultimate fulfillment – discovered that there is happiness, a complete fulfilment available to every human being within oneself and independent of anything outside. The search just has to be reversed to look within!
author: Sri M

text: In matters beyond the rational mind, realisation takes place only when the rational mind becomes absolutely still. To find that out, we need a rational mind!
author: Sri M

text: If the world were a complete obstruction to the attainment of spiritual fulfillment, the Supreme Being would not have created it at all. The world exists around us and also in our minds to make us understand, learn, grow and become complete.
author: Sri M

text: In this material world – earning one’s living, going through all the problems and travails of worldly, mundane existence is a necessary step in learning about spiritual consciousness and evolution to higher levels
author: Sri M

text: Don’t run away from the battle. Stay there and fight it out – but with love, affection, and understanding.
author: Sri M

text: The secret of visualization – creative thought, is to actually believe and picture it as one wants, as if already there. When the mind is open and when there is a great desire to achieve something then the channels for achieving it are opened.
author: Sri M

text: Babaji used to say, ‘The seeds have been planted, they have been sown but no seed will become a tree and bear fruit in three days, it takes its own time’. So sow the seed, keep the climate clear, water it properly, and then we’ll see what happens.
author: Sri M

text: I am not denying that we need a rational mind to find this realization. The rational mind has to understand that there is only a limit to which it can go and after that, it has to stop and become quiet. In that quietness, the other manifests itself.
author: Sri M

text: Living in this world and experiencing life, I would say is the philosopher’s stone, which eventually can purify you from base metal to pure gold.
author: Sri M

text: I think all the sadhana we do is intended to mostly bring about the hunger for God – for that Truth. When that hunger has built up, then God is at your doorstep!
author: Sri M

text: Any pleasures of the senses will always have some pain behind it. The greatest pain is to lose the pleasure we are enjoying.
author: Sri M

text: We can’t live on our past heritage alone; we must look at the now. The entire spiritual movement, scientific progress, is based on the understanding that ‘I don’t know’.
author: Sri M

text: Surrender means to understand that I am helpless at a certain point and, therefore, I need to relax, let go, be patient, and wait. In that waiting, something arrives. The breeze may be from within.
author: Sri M

text: It’s more important to understand the teachings than to worship the teacher. The sacred is always around us and in our hearts.
author: Sri M

text: We carry so many things in our head. Be simple. Throw off the burdens and be free!
author: Sri M

text: What is spirituality? It is to find the truth, to find yourself, to find who you are, and what your link with Supreme Being is.
author: Sri M

text: The greatest miracle is to bring about a transformation in thinking, to turn inward, and try to figure out what life is all about. What is our link with life? What is life itself? Whether I am here just to be born and die, is there something more than this.
author: Sri M

text: Any place, where the truth is worshipped, is a temple for us. The most important temple is the body. Inside us is the heart where the Truth sits.
author: Sri M

text: I decided, ‘I am walking on this path, it’s a lonely path’. Like Jesus Christ said, 'It’s a straight and narrow path’. So, let’s stick to it and not get side-tracked.
author: Sri M

text: Jesus said the real treasure is in your heart where thieves do not break in and steal; It is this treasure that we seek.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual teacher sometimes provides opportunities or situations deliberately or as they happen. He does not encourage people to run away from them but to pause and remain. It is only when faced with a situation, one begins to realize where one stands.
author: Sri M

text: If I say I know everything, then there is no movement, research, or inquiry. It is what we don’t know that inspires us to search and move forward.
author: Sri M

text: What is that one learns in the grihastha phase which is different from brahmacharya ? Once you are married you have one more person in your life; you cannot take independent and exclusive decisions. You learn to restrain your emotions and to look at the other person’s point of view.
author: Sri M

text: Once I examine myself and find there are things to be improved, the first move is to take a positive step to improve and the second, do your sadhana seriously. These are two essentials that have to go hand in hand.
author: Sri M

text: Happiness is a universal search. Whether one is a believer or a non–believer, Hindu, Muslim, Christian, or Sikh – everybody looks for happiness in this world. All our attempts to grasp things and hold on to them are the search for happiness.
author: Sri M

text: On New Year’s Eve, note down point-by-point negative habits in ourselves that we need to overcome. As you wake up to a new dawn, go through them carefully, and implement ways to get free of these. It can be done! The only way to get rid of negativity is to bring in positivity.
author: Sri M
